correctness.rationale: The three-round Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé invariant is the nested set of root/pair atomic incidence types including all possible third-vertex five-bit masks; equality and repetitions are explicitly accounted for. A third move sees only the four nearest neighboring candidates plus existence of a distant loop/nonloop, so cycle lengths at least seven collapse to seven; three copies of any component length suffice when at most three distinct components can be selected. Those infinite reductions are distinct from the finite census. An independently implemented full-vertex direct signature routine agreed with the local-signature method on all 731 canonical vectors of order at most 19; separate enumeration of all 4^7-1=16,383 reduced vectors gave exactly 143 distinct signatures and 142 signatures at order<=18. The sole first appearance at order 19 was multiplicities (3,2,1,1,1,0,0). The finite enumeration exhausts its proved reduced domain; it is not extrapolated to the unrestricted domain without the reduction proof.
